extraQa: Can I still file a warranty claim on my Titan Solar panels or inverter?

Yes, in most cases. The panel and inverter warranties come from the equipment manufacturer, not from Titan, so they generally still apply. What is gone is Titan's own workmanship warranty. A claim usually needs the serial number, the install date and proof of the problem, such as an error code or production data. We gather those and handle the claim and the replacement work.
How do I know if my Titan Solar system is still producing?

Compare this month's production in your inverter's monitoring app with the same month last year, and look for a bill that has crept up. An app that shows zero, an inverter light that is red or flashing, or one panel or string far below the rest are the usual warning signs. If you are not sure, a free evaluation compares what the system should produce with what it actually produces.
titan.html:
What Titan Solar customers should do now

Titan Solar Power filed Chapter 7 liquidation in June 2024. That ended the company, so there is no Titan support line, no Titan service crew and no Titan to honor its own workmanship warranty. Your panels, inverter and any battery still work, and the equipment manufacturers' warranties generally still apply. What you have lost is the person who would diagnose a problem, file the claim and do the labor.

Step 1: find out what is on your roof

Photograph the label on the inverter (it lists the brand, model and serial number), a label on the back of one panel if you can see it, and the sticker on your main service panel. Note which monitoring app you use. Those four things tell us which manufacturer warranty applies.

Step 2: check that it is producing

Open the monitoring app and compare this month with the same month last year. Check your utility bill too. A system that stopped producing quietly can cost hundreds of dollars a year before anyone notices. Our guide to SolarEdge inverter error codes and our Enphase troubleshooting guide explain what common fault messages mean.

Step 3: keep paying any loan or lease

The company that financed your system is separate from Titan. Keep making payments and keep your loan or lease papers handy for the evaluation.

Step 4: book an independent evaluation

We start with your photos and your utility bill, then schedule a technician visit or a guided video evaluation. The first evaluation is free. Read the full guide: Titan Solar went out of business: what happens to my system?

We service Titan systems across San Diego, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside and San Bernardino counties.

extraQa: Does the 25-year SunPower panel warranty still count after the bankruptcy?

Usually yes for the panels themselves. The product and power warranty on SunPower-brand and Maxeon panels is backed by the panel manufacturer rather than the installer, so it generally survives. The bundled service and workmanship coverage is the part that depended on SunPower still operating. A claim still needs someone to diagnose the fault and do the replacement work.
Can I add a battery to my existing SunPower system?

Often yes. Whether it works, and what it costs, depends on whether your system uses microinverters or a string inverter and how your panel is set up. A free evaluation checks that and tells you what a battery would and would not do for your bill before you decide anything.

What SunPower customers should do now

SunPower Corporation filed Chapter 11 in August 2024 and sold off its business units. Pieces of the residential business were bought and the SunPower name is still in use, but the original company that installed and serviced most existing rooftops no longer works the way it did. Your panels are still producing, and the manufacturer's panel warranty generally still applies. The gap is service: someone to diagnose, file the claim and do the labor.

Step 1: identify your equipment

Photograph the inverter or microinverter label, a panel label if visible, and the sticker on your main service panel. Your paperwork may show SunPower, Complete Solar or BRS Field Ops on the permit or contract, depending on when and how it was installed.

Step 2: check production

Compare this month in the monitoring app with the same month last year, and look at your electric bill. If a microinverter or a panel string stops, the app may keep running while production quietly drops. Our Enphase microinverter troubleshooting guide covers the common causes.

Step 3: keep paying any loan or lease

A loan, lease or PPA is a separate contract from the installer. Keep making payments and bring the documents to the evaluation.

Step 4: get an independent evaluation

We start with your photos and utility bill, then schedule a technician visit or a guided video evaluation. The first evaluation is free. Read the full guide: SunPower went bankrupt: what happens to my panels and warranty?

We service SunPower systems across San Diego, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside and San Bernardino counties.
